title: `await` inside a loop over independent I/O multiplies latency by N — batch the API call or Promise.all the fetches
trigger: Perf audit or a data path that scales with item count (N cards, N terms, N files, N resources) and feels slow under real payloads
principle: Sequential `await` per item turns roundtrip cost into N×RTT (or N transactions). If the items are independent, collapse them: one batched API call (multi-id request), Promise.all over fetches, or a single-IDB-transaction writer. Preserve ordering/failure semantics explicitly — parallelize the I/O, keep validation sequential. For pipelines, prefetch depth-1 so the next fetch overlaps the current import. Inverting a filter condition during such a rewrite is the classic regression — re-check skip-vs-keep polarity before committing.

cases.context: Anki status write-back queue called cardsInfo per card and setWordStatusFromSync per term — hundreds of serial RTTs + one IDB tx per term on every sync cycle
cases.bad: for (const t of queue) { const info = await cardsInfo(t.cardId); ... } for (const u of updates) await setWordStatusFromSync(...)
cases.good: const infos = await cardsInfo(allIds) (per-card fallback on failure) → collect updates → await setWordStatusesFromSync(lang, updates) — one tx, one broadcast

cases.context: Commons audio search fetched file info for ≤10 titles serially — user waits RTT×10 for the audio list
cases.bad: for (const r of results.slice(0,10)) items.push(await fetchCommonsFileInfo(r.title))
cases.good: const infos = await Promise.all(results.slice(0,10).map(r => fetchCommonsFileInfo(r.title))); then validate/build sequentially over resolved infos
